findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects including the seeded vendor roster are stored without an enforced default encryption policy or KMS key.
No ACL is declared and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the bucket has no explicit private access boundary and could be exposed by a later ACL or bucket policy grant.
No logging block is configured, so read and write access to this bucket and the vendor roster object it holds leaves no server access log trail for detecting unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed with no recoverable prior version, enabling destructive tampering.
This ledger export bucket, which by name holds financial records, has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data is stored without enforced default encryption.
No logging block is configured for this sensitive financial export bucket, so object-level access is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a subsequent bucket policy or ACL change from exposing the financial data publicly.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, allowing silent overwrite or permanent deletion of ledger export objects with no recovery.

The model artifacts bucket defines no default server-side encryption, so stored artifacts are not protected by an enforced encryption policy or KMS key, unlike the audit_trail bucket in the same file.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so public ACLs or bucket policies could later be applied without being blocked at the bucket boundary.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks routinely contain sensitive procedural, connection, and access details stored without enforced encryption.
No logging block is defined, so reads and modifications of operational documentation are not recorded to the audit_trail bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the private ACL is the sole control preventing public exposure and can be overridden by a later policy or ACL change.

The audit log destination bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no object lock, MFA delete, or public access block, so the entire retained audit trail can be deleted in a single apply and log integrity rests only on versioning.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The central log-delivery bucket has no access logging of its own, so access to or tampering with the collected audit logs is not independently recorded.

A vendor roster spreadsheet, likely containing third-party business contact or PII data, is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument and no explicit private ACL, into a bucket that itself lacks default encryption and any public access block.
